cards.front: Recall a key point about Polymers in Engineering
cards.back: Thermoplastics soften when heated and harden when cooled; they can be repeatedly reshaped (e.g. ABS, acrylic, nylon, polycarbonate, polypropylene).

cards.front: Recall a key point about Polymers in Engineering
cards.back: Thermosetting polymers undergo an irreversible chemical change when heated; they cannot be remelted (e.g. epoxy resin, melamine formaldehyde, polyester resin).

cards.front: Recall a key point about Polymers in Engineering
cards.back: Elastomers are polymers with elastic properties; vulcanised rubber is the most common engineering elastomer.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Polymers in Engineering
cards.back: ABS is tough, impact-resistant and easily injection-moulded; used for enclosures, car interiors and consumer products.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Polymers in Engineering
cards.back: Nylon has excellent wear resistance, low friction and good mechanical strength; used for gears, bearings and bushes.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Polymers in Engineering
cards.back: Polycarbonate is extremely impact-resistant and transparent; used for safety visors, machine guards and electronic housings.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Polymers in Engineering
cards.back: Epoxy resin is a thermoset with excellent adhesive properties and chemical resistance; used for composite matrices and coatings.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Polymers in Engineering
cards.back: Polymer selection depends on mechanical requirements, operating temperature, chemical exposure, cost and processing method.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Polymers in Engineering
cards.back: Thermoplastics are generally recyclable because they can be remelted; thermosets are not easily recycled.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Polymers in Engineering
cards.back: Injection moulding is the primary manufacturing process for thermoplastic engineering components.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Polymers in Engineering
cards.back: Polymer properties change with temperature: most thermoplastics soften above their glass transition temperature (Tg).

cards.front: Recall a key point about Polymers in Engineering
cards.back: Additives (plasticisers, fillers, stabilisers, colourants) modify polymer properties for specific applications.

cards.front: What should you know about gcse engineering exam tips — polymers in engineering?
cards.back: 1. For Polymers in Engineering questions, use precise design and technology terminology 2. Consider function, aesthetics, ergonomics, sustainability and cost in your answers 3. When evaluating, justify your design decisions with reference to user needs and specifications 4. Show your understanding of Polymers in Engineering through both theory and practical application 5. Reference real products and manufacturing processes where relevant
